scope: One frozen exhaustive B2 OR-pair candidate followed by the frozen roots_only exact capped elimination in a reachable root-phase state.

definitions.N: fixed normalized root input size units
definitions.n: number of live variables in F
definitions.b: a nondegenerate literal on another variable that co-occurs with a
definitions.t: number of clauses containing both a and b

lemma.statement: If B_drain <= N^2, then the frozen exhaustive v2 grammar has an admitted exact strict-progress root rescue at this state no later than candidate (a,b) in canonical pair order.
proof: Frozen v2 deterministically enumerates every nondegenerate sign-aware literal pair that co-occurs in a live clause, so candidate (a,b) is eventually considered unless an earlier candidate already succeeds.

apply_or_pair_v2 replaces every clause containing both a and b by a clause in which both literals are absent and fresh -e is present, and adds exactly the three B2 definition clauses (-e,-a), (-e,-b), (e,a,b).

Every one of the t replaced clauses loses one literal relative to its source clause; the three definition clauses contribute 7 literal occurrences and 3 clauses. Before any extra canonical subsumption benefit, this gives state_units(macro) <= s - t + 10.

All t replaced clauses contained signed literal a. After replacement they contain neither a nor -a. Among the three definitions, exactly (e,a,b) contains a and exactly (-e,-a) contains -a. Canonical duplicate/subsumption reduction can only remove occurrences. Therefore the post-macro pivot incidences satisfy c_sigma' <= c_sigma - t + 1 and c_opp' <= c_opp + 1.

The macro introduces at most the one fresh extension e, so it has at most n+1 live variables. Eliminating root variable x leaves at most n live variables; every non-tautological canonical resolvent therefore has width at most n and contributes at most n+1 state units including its clause-count unit.
The exact resolution parent-pair count for x is at most c_sigma'*c_opp' <= (c_sigma-t+1)*(c_opp+1). Unique non-tautological resolvents cannot exceed the number of parent pairs.

The retained raw representation before adding resolvents is a subrepresentation of the macro CNF, hence its state units are <= state_units(macro). Consequently raw_units(eliminate x from macro) <= s-t+10 + (n+1)*(c_sigma-t+1)*(c_opp+1) = B_drain.

If B_drain<=N^2, the macro itself also fits the N^2 cap and the exact elimination of x cannot abort above N^2. The independent exact transition verifier therefore has a valid roots_only pivot available. first_capped_elimination may choose an earlier canonical live root pivot instead; that is already a root rescue, so discovery succeeds no later than x.

Frozen progress_phi gives every surviving original root variable a coefficient len(root_vars)+extension_cap+1, strictly larger than the possible one-variable change in ordinary live-variable count. A successful roots_only elimination removes an original root while B2 adds at most one non-root extension, hence after_phi < before_phi. Thus the frozen strict-progress gate passes.
Therefore the frozen candidate is an exact admitted v2 root rescue.

important_difference_from_frequent_pair_.old_sufficient_mechanism: Require t >= s-2N+11 so the entire macro falls into the <=2N-1 corridor where some root pivot is guaranteed to fit.
important_difference_from_frequent_pair_.new_sufficient_mechanism: The macro may remain very large. It is enough that replacing t occurrences of one signed root literal makes that root variable's own post-macro resolution product fit the fixed N^2 cap.
important_difference_from_frequent_pair_.relation: Neither sufficient condition is claimed necessary.

new_totality_candidate.statement: Every reachable root-phase state in which all ordinary pivots overflow N^2 contains some co-occurring pair (a,b), with a a signed literal of a live original root variable, satisfying B_drain(a,b)<=N^2.
